items.name: Claude Haiku 5.5 — Anthropic
items.summary: Anthropic's cheapest, fastest small model ever — ~75% cheaper to run than Haiku 4.5, the first Haiku with an adjustable effort setting, and it beats OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna on Anthropic's benchmarks (OSWorld 2.1: 72.4% vs 48.9%).

items.name: Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk") — Mistral AI
items.summary: Mistral's largest model ever: a 1T-parameter natively multimodal MoE (52B active), pitched as the strongest open-weight model built outside China, trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in European datacenters.

items.name: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI — OpenAI
items.summary: OpenAI rolled GPT-6 snapshots to all 1.2B+ weekly ChatGPT users with "Intelligent UI" — answers composed from text, visuals, and interactive elements per question — plus GPT-6 Instant starting web-search answers 44% sooner than GPT-5.6 Instant.

items.name: Beam — Reflection AI
items.summary: The Nvidia-backed startup's first open-weight model: a 501B-parameter text-only sparse MoE (23B active per token) for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads, trained on 10.5K NVIDIA GB300 GPUs; Apache 2.0 weights promised later in October.

items.name: Clef — Cloudflare
items.summary: A pair of open-weight decision models (27B multimodal + 9B Clef-Flash) for decision-making rather than text generation — they return probabilities per option in a single forward pass, aimed at agent hot-paths like ticket routing and bot filtering.
